chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Ibn Riʾāb, from Ḍurays al-Kunāsī, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

"No remission is granted for the hudud that belong to Allah apart from the Imam. But as for what pertains to the rights of the people within a hadd, there is no harm in its being remitted apart from the Imam."

key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam, the rightful authority over enforcement and remission in such matters
key_terms.الْحُدُودِ: the prescribed legal punishments or penal limits in sacred law
key_terms.حَقِّ النَّاسِ: the rights of people, meaning claims belonging to individuals
key_terms.لِلَّهِ: belonging to Allah, referring to divine right

ai.seo_question: Can hadd punishments be forgiven in cases involving Allah’s rights and people’s rights?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes between hudud related to the right of Allah and those involving the rights of people. It states that remission of Allah’s hudud is not permitted without the Imam, while remission in matters tied to people’s rights is permissible without the Imam.
